messages:
Maya: Hey team — draft for qprofile packaging & naming that ties into Redwood Optimize reco engine. TL;DR: single manifest per profile, fields for quant backend (gptq/awq/fp8/int8), accuracy_delta, perf_metrics, target_deploy_profile, and semantic tags. Example below.

Tony: Can you paste the manifest example? Also how do we version compat between backend changes and model patches?

Maya: Sure — manifest example:
```yaml
qprofile_version: "1.0"
model: "llama-2-13b"
profile_id: "llama-2-13b/awq-v1"
backend: "AWQ"
quant_bits: 8
accuracy_delta: "-0.6%"    # vs fp32 on mix-bench
perf_rps: "+120%"
target_deploy_profile: "dedicated-low-latency"
recommended_batching: "0|0|16"   # min|p50|max
notes: "use grouped-floats tweak for long context"
```

Emily: Quick data — AWQ v1 on llama-2-13b showed -0.6% rouge on summarization eval, INT8-GPTQ showed -0.4% but had ~30% higher token throughput vs AWQ. FP8 had near-zero delta on 2-shot but needs custom kernels.

Sanjay: For 'target_deploy_profile' we should map to actual infra pools: hosted, dedicated-small, dedicated-large, private-vpc. Recommend we include a 'cost_index' integer so Optimize can tradeoff.

Maya: Good call — propose adding cost_index and 'compat_tags' list to indicate which runtime kernels are required (e.g., cuda>=12.3, cuBLASLt, custom-kernel-v2).

Tony: Versioning note: qprofile_version + semantic profile_id (consumer-facing) + internal build tag. CI must refuse qprofiles that reference incompatible kernels.

ci-bot: CI: qprofile lint passed for profile_id "llama-2-13b/awq-v1" — tests: format, schema, sample-inference

Kevin: How do we surface accuracy_delta to customers? In Optimize UI we can show a small delta badge with tooltip linking to the evaluation shard. Also gating rule: only publish profiles with delta > -2.0% in default public catalog.

Emily: Also recommend 'eval_hooks' pointer to the eval set & seed used so results are reproducible. Example: eval_hook: "s3://redwood-evals/llama-2-13b/awq-v1/summary.json"

Sanjay: Operational: include 'kv_cache_policy' and 'prefetch' booleans in manifest so serving runtime applies correct cache behavior.

Maya: OK I'll update the draft with cost_index, compat_tags, eval_hooks, kv_cache_policy. Next steps: implement linter rule in repo, create small CSV export for Optimize ingestion, and schedule a canary deploy. Anyone volunteer to own the linter PR?

Tony: I'll take the linter PR. Will coordinate with eng-infra for kernel validation.

Emily: I'll prepare the eval shard and add the reproducible run notebook to s3.

Kevin: I'll add the rollout checklist and canary gates to the runbook.

Maya: sweet — assigning owners. I'll push the manifest template to docs and add examples for FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ comparisons. :rocket:

Tony: one last Q — naming: prefer lowercase slash separated like 'model/backend-vN' or dotted like 'model.backend.vN'? I'm leaning slash.

Maya: slash wins for readability and path compatibility. agreed.

ci-bot: Deploy: scheduled canary for qprofile-catalog ingestion at 2025-12-03T17:30:00Z

Kevin: Thanks all — let's try to close PRs by EOD Friday.
